_policy: Objects that hardware reads or writes on its own, so that a volatile qualifier on them is evidence, not steering, wherever tools/volatile_rom_proof.py shows the qualifier's effect on their accesses. A dma-source or dma-target entry names a RAM object (a data symbol, its mapped address and its size) and ROM code that programs a DMA channel with it: the code's bytes are pinned by SHA-256 and the transfer is read off the instructions at every run. A scanline-payload-getter entry names a function whose pinned code returns a scanline task's payload, read off its instructions and its two callees' at every run, with the scanline pipeline that hands the payload to the HBlank DMA bank. Listing an object admits nothing by itself. ONLY the repository maintainer may add an entry; agents park the function and cite the evidence instead.

entries.reason: two banks of 128 OAM entries (8 bytes each), selected by data_03000028 and counted by data_03000020; the OAM flush 080012BC loads 0x03000030 (pool word 080014B0), adds the inactive bank's offset (bank << 10) and stores it to DMA0SAD at 080013D4, the OAM cursor to DMA0DAD, and 0x84000000 | (count * 2) to DMA0CNT at 080013E0

the blend display task's scanline payload: 080D9A24 creates the task with event callback 080D96F0, whose event 0 stores the 0800D61C scanline task in the task data word +4; 080D9B08 returns 0800C614 of that word, the BLDALPHA rows 0800DB0C writes (tools/blend_ramp.py) and the scanline manager 0800C4B4 converts into the HBlank DMA bank

the window task's scanline payload: 080DAB84 creates the task with event callback 080D9C58, whose event 0 allocates the WIN0H/WIN1H scanline task and stores it in the task data word +4; 080DABB4 returns 0800C614 of that word, the WINxH rows tools/window_scanline.py's writers fill and the scanline manager 0800C4B4 converts into the HBlank DMA bank
